answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring costful on-ledger history before an identity may transact: each new agent must complete a verifiable job — for example, attesting a shipment of ferrous scrap along a canyon rail depot — before its key is minted. Without that ledger-stamped record, a swarm of fake identities cannot spend, because merchants only accept keys whose attestation chain anchors above the trust ledge of the ledger. Sockpuppets pile up below the ledge; real economic weight lives above it.
